note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a ARM 13; A06b ARM 13; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 3 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Dual citizenship restriction), A01b (descent, born abroad: Dual citizenship restriction), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a dual-citizenship restriction on descent, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: ARLIS (Armenian Legal Information System), Law of the Republic of Armenia on the Citizenship of the Republic of Armenia HO-16, with changes by HO-408-N of 11 December 2023 (English), Articles 1, 11, 13. Every figure the file holds now rests on it, and the dataset is no longer cited. Article 11's limit on a child of one citizen and one foreign parent replaced the dataset's wording of the limit abroad.

sources.title: ARLIS (Armenian Legal Information System), Law of the Republic of Armenia on the Citizenship of the Republic of Armenia HO-16, with changes by HO-408-N of 11 December 2023 (English), Articles 1, 11, 13
sources.said: Article 1 ... Renouncing the citizenship of the Republic of Armenia or accepting the citizenship of another State shall not per se entail forfeiture of the citizenship of the Republic of Armenia. ... Article 11 ... A child, whose parents are citizens of the Republic of Armenia at the moment of his or her birth, shall acquire the citizenship of the Republic of Armenia, regardless of the place of birth. ... Where at the moment of a child's birth, one of the parents is a citizen of the Republic of Armenia and the other parent is a foreign citizen, the citizenship of the child shall be determined upon a written consent of the parents. In the absence of consent, the child shall acquire the citizenship of the Republic of Armenia, if he or she was born in the Republic of Armenia, or if in case of not acquiring the citizenship of the Republic of Armenia, the child becomes a stateless person, or if the parents permanently reside in the Republic of Armenia. ... Article 13 ... (1) has been permanently residing in the Republic of Armenia for the last three years as prescribed by law; (2) may express himself or herself in Armenian and (3) is familiar with the Constitution of the Republic of Armenia.

atBirth.descentAbroad: A child of one citizen and one foreign parent born abroad takes it on the parents' written consent, or without it only if it would otherwise be stateless or the parents permanently reside in Armenia.
